claims.claim: Every Astro command takes --verbose, --silent and --json logging flags; under jet dev, --verbose was accepted and printed nothing extra in our capture, though the ratified dashboard gives --verbose a meaning.
claims.incremental_contribution: Shows the verbosity ladder incumbents put on every verb and that jet dev --verbose is currently inert.

claims.claim: astro --help lists only commands that work; jet help lists `jet dev --canvas|--app|--share` forms that all refuse with E2104 "not built yet".
claims.incremental_contribution: Help text advertising refused forms is a first-hour trap no incumbent sets.

claims.claim: astro dev takes --port, --host and --open on the verb itself; `jet dev --port 5317` was read as a file ("E2105 Can't securely read the file `5317`") and `--open` was silently ignored.
claims.incremental_contribution: Port, host and open flags are table stakes in every incumbent; Jet's ratified settings table (D-SETTING-ORDER1) already shows --port but the parser does not take it.

claims.claim: Astro runs the dev server in the background with stop, status and logs --follow subcommands, so a second shell or an agent can find and stop it.
claims.incremental_contribution: Introduces a managed-lifetime pattern Jet has no answer to; jet dev only runs in the foreground.

claims.claim: astro build --timings reports where build time went; `jet build --target web` printed nothing on success in our capture.
claims.incremental_contribution: A silent successful build gives no output path, size or time; incumbents always print at least the output summary.

claims.claim: Astro keeps type checking out of the dev server (astro check --watch); jet dev reports type errors inline with Why/Fix (E0113) before rerunning.
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms a Jet lead: checked errors during dev without a second watcher process.

claims.claim: astro info prints toolchain versions, OS, package manager and integrations for bug reports and can copy them; jet help shows only `jet version`.
claims.incremental_contribution: A one-command environment report shortens every bug report; Jet has the facts (compiler identity, target) but no dump verb was found.

claims.claim: Astro separates per-user preferences (.astro/settings.json, --global) from shared project config, so one developer can hide the toolbar without changing the team file.
claims.incremental_contribution: Relevant to where a Jet dev-dashboard toggle would live; spec places dashboard toggles in session keys, not project config.

claims.claim: astro preferences list has --json output so tools can read the effective dev settings.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet ratified `--json` jet.status/v1 for rebuild events; a settings dump is not covered.

claims.claim: astro dev logs --follow streams a background server's log, like tail -f.
claims.incremental_contribution: Only useful with a background mode; included in the agent-status card draft.

claims.claim: Astro binds localhost unless --host is passed and warns never to expose dev servers in production; jet dev binds 127.0.0.1 by default (JET_APP_PORT, Core/Web/Web.jet).
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms Jet's safe default; Next.js and Deno bind 0.0.0.0 by default.

claims.claim: Astro and Vite restrict the Host header (--allowed-hosts / server.allowedHosts) to block DNS rebinding against a local dev server.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's dev server answers any Host on 127.0.0.1 [INFERENCE: not probed]; a rebinding page could read dev responses.

claims.claim: Astro auto-detects AI agents and switches dev to background mode with a lock file (URL, PID), JSON logs and a health endpoint; a second `astro dev` prints the running URL and PID instead of failing.
claims.incremental_contribution: Strongest agent-first dev-server design seen; Jet's ratified /__jet_dev_status endpoint could carry the same facts.

claims.claim: Astro injects a dev toolbar into every page during dev; Jet's ratified design has a browser corner strip and overlay, but jet dev serves pages with no injected client at all.
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms the ratified browser strip is the right shape and shows Jet has none of it today.

claims.claim: The toolbar menu copies environment debug info for bug reports in one click.
claims.incremental_contribution: Pairs with astro info; Jet has neither.

claims.claim: Astro's Inspect app shows each island's props and hydration directive on the page.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet hydrates #Target(Web) islands; an inspector would show which nodes run client-side.

claims.claim: Astro audits accessibility and performance in dev with a visible red dot; Jet has `jet lint --a11y` but nothing in the dev browser.
claims.incremental_contribution: Moves an existing Jet check into the dev surface.

claims.claim: Integrations extend the Astro toolbar with their own apps via an API.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's ratified #DevPanel/dev plugin direction (#4275) matches; no new work beyond it.

claims.claim: Bun maps routes to HTML entries and bundles on request inside the user's own Bun.serve; Jet's web.app().route(...) serves SSR pages from Jet functions in the same process.
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms Jet's single-process server+page model matches the newest incumbent.

claims.claim: With development.console: true Bun streams browser console.log/error to the terminal over the HMR WebSocket; jet dev shows no browser output.
claims.incremental_contribution: Browser-side failures of #Target(Web) code are invisible in the jet dev terminal.

claims.claim: Bun's dev mode opens one WebSocket (/_bun/hmr) per tab for updates and console traffic; we measured 24 ms edit-to-browser.
claims.incremental_contribution: One push channel serves both reload and console forwarding; feeds the push-vs-poll ballot.

claims.claim: Bun documents a dev vs prod behavior table (rebundle on request, sourcemaps, error page vs cached minified bundles).
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet docs lack an equivalent jet dev vs jet run vs jet build table for web.

claims.claim: Bun declares dev-server plugins statically in bunfig rather than in executable config.
claims.incremental_contribution: Matches Jet's preference for declarative project settings; no gap.

claims.claim: Bun and Vite only inline env variables with a public prefix (PUBLIC_*, VITE_*) into browser bundles to avoid leaking secrets.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's #Target(Web) code reading environment needs the same guard; ownership sits with the web platform card.

claims.claim: Bun links sourcemaps in dev so browser stacks point at source; Jet browser code is wasm plus jet_dom_runtime.js and our captures never produced a browser stack to judge.
claims.incremental_contribution: Source-mapped browser errors are an open evidence gap for Jet web.

claims.claim: Bun.serve takes an error() hook that turns a thrown handler into a custom response, and dev shows a code-framed error page while the server keeps running (we exercised a 500 then a 200).
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet has no per-request error hook; a panicking handler ends the whole dev server.

claims.claim: Bun states SSR is not built in; Jet's web.app().route(...).ssr(...) renders server-side out of the box.
claims.incremental_contribution: A Jet lead over Bun's fullstack server.

claims.claim: Bun offers two reload tiers: --watch (process restart) and --hot (in-place module rerun keeping the socket); jet dev only restarts.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's ratified #Persist hot state (D-DEV-STATE1, #6386) is the planned second tier.

claims.claim: Bun type-checks before restart only with --check; jet dev always checks first and keeps the error on screen (E0113 Why/Fix).
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet lead: checking is the default, not a flag.

claims.claim: Bun exposes --no-clear-screen and --watch-kill-signal for long-lived children.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's dev loop has no documented signal choice for the child [INFERENCE from help text].

claims.claim: Under --hot, Bun keeps globalThis and the listening server so counters and caches survive an edit; jet dev restarts the app, so in-memory state resets.
claims.incremental_contribution: Feeds the #Persist card: state survival is the default job users expect.

claims.claim: Bun admits its soft reload re-transpiles everything and is unoptimized, yet we measured 24 ms edit-to-browser; jet dev took 1525 ms edit-to-server.
claims.incremental_contribution: Bounds how far Jet trails even an unoptimized reload path.

claims.claim: deno serve owns the listener and calls a user fetch handler; Jet's .serve() likewise owns the socket in Core/Web.
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms the Jet-owned server runtime direction (#4635).

claims.claim: Deno documents that a throwing handler fails only that request (we saw 500 then 200); a panicking Jet handler killed the jet dev server for every later request.
claims.incremental_contribution: Direct evidence for #4635 c1.

claims.claim: deno serve binds 0.0.0.0:8000 by default; jet dev binds 127.0.0.1.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet is safer by default; LAN sharing is opt-in (--share lan, ratified, unbuilt).

claims.claim: deno serve --parallel runs one isolate per core behind one port.
claims.incremental_contribution: Not a dev-loop need; noted for production parity only.

claims.claim: Expo start prints a QR code, the URL and a single-key shortcut list without Enter; jet dev prints no URL and treats typed keys as ordinary input (h/r/o/q echoed).
claims.incremental_contribution: Best-in-class terminal UI; Jet ratified single keys (D-RUN-SESSION1) but jet dev has none.

claims.claim: Expo defaults to the LAN address so a phone can scan and connect; Jet ratified --share lan but `jet dev --app run --share lan` refuses with E2104.
claims.incremental_contribution: Phone testing of #Target(Web) pages needs LAN plus a printed QR.

claims.claim: Expo accepts --port 0 to take any free port and prints the chosen one.
claims.incremental_contribution: A clean answer to port conflicts without silent fallback.

claims.claim: Expo tunnels add a random subdomain so a public URL is not guessable.
claims.incremental_contribution: If Jet ever adds tunnel sharing, the token in the ratified --share lan --token design plays the same role.

claims.claim: Expo exposes /_expo/open so agents and scripts can do what the terminal keys do; Jet ratified /__jet_dev_status as the dashboard's single source.
claims.incremental_contribution: A key-equivalent HTTP surface is the agent-friendly twin of session keys.

claims.claim: The open endpoint treats GET as a side-effect-free dry run and refuses cross-origin POST with 403.
claims.incremental_contribution: Any Jet dev control endpoint needs the same origin guard.

claims.claim: The endpoint distinguishes 501 (cannot launch from this host) from 500 (launch failed).
claims.incremental_contribution: Typed status codes for tools match Jet's typed-error stance.

claims.claim: Expo filters thousands of native build log lines down to the errors in the user's own files and pipes simulator logs into the same terminal.
claims.incremental_contribution: Same principle as forwarding browser console and runtime errors to the jet dev terminal.

claims.claim: Expo, Vite (--base) and Rsbuild (server.base) let the app run under a sub-path; Jet web.app has no documented base path [INFERENCE: not probed].
claims.incremental_contribution: Matters when a Jet app sits behind a reverse proxy.

claims.claim: expo config --json prints the fully evaluated project config for tools and agents.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet has --json on several verbs; an evaluated dev-settings dump would show which of --port/d.port/default won (D-SETTING-ORDER1 note line covers part).

claims.claim: expo install --check flags dependency versions that do not match the SDK.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet locks dependencies and has jet fetch/update; no gap for dev.

claims.claim: Expo documents every CLI behavior switch as an environment variable (no QR, debug logs, offline).
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet documents JET_APP_PORT/JET_DEV_PORT in source but not in jet help dev.

claims.claim: Expo turns off keys and prompts when CI=1 or stdin is not a TTY.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's ratified dashboard already falls back to plain lines without a TTY.

claims.claim: Expo, Astro and Next.js overlays open the failing file in $EDITOR from the error; Jet diagnostics give file:line but nothing opens it.
claims.incremental_contribution: Click-to-open closes the loop from overlay to fix.

claims.claim: next dev binds 0.0.0.0 by default and prints a Network URL (we saw http://192.168.0.77:5410); jet dev binds 127.0.0.1 and prints nothing.
claims.incremental_contribution: Next shows the LAN URL; Jet should print at least the local URL (ratified) and keep LAN opt-in.

claims.claim: next dev --experimental-https creates a locally trusted certificate; Parcel and Vite offer self-signed HTTPS too; jet dev has no HTTPS option.
claims.incremental_contribution: Needed for secure-context browser APIs and cookies; low priority for first-hour users.

claims.claim: next dev --experimental-cpu-prof and vite --profile profile the dev server itself; Jet has jet perf but no documented dev-server profile flag.
claims.incremental_contribution: Helps diagnose the 1.5 s Jet edit cycle and ~1 GB RSS.

claims.claim: Next keeps dev output in .next/dev separate from build output so both run concurrently.
claims.incremental_contribution: Whether jet dev and jet build share artifacts safely was not probed.

claims.claim: next build ends with a per-route table (static/dynamic, size); `jet build --target web` printed nothing and wrote no index.html.
claims.incremental_contribution: A silent build is the worst first-hour signal; incumbents always summarize output.

claims.claim: next upgrade --agent delegates codemod-driven upgrades to a coding agent.
claims.incremental_contribution: Agent-first tooling is a trend; Jet's jet fix/jet update cover upgrades without an agent hook.

claims.claim: next analyze offers a bundle graph UI and JSONL export; Jet ratified a code map/treemap view under #4275.
claims.incremental_contribution: Covered by planned Jet work; Jet's web output is one wasm plus runtime (rt.wasm about 4.26 MB).

claims.claim: next build --debug-prerender keeps going to show every prerender error; jet dev shows all errors but a single parse slip produced a 5-problem cascade (E0003 ×4 + E0083).
claims.incremental_contribution: Root-cause-first ordering matters more than count; #3720 c28-29 owns the cascade.

claims.claim: Next documents that PORT in .env is ignored because the server binds before env files load.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's ratified note line (`--port=4000 replaces d.port(3000)`) is the better pattern: say which setting won.

claims.claim: Next names CPU profile files per process so dev, build and start profiles do not overwrite each other.
claims.incremental_contribution: Minor; relevant only once jet dev gains a profile flag.

claims.claim: Next shows a corner indicator per page (static or dynamic route, issue count badge "1 Issue"); jet dev pages carry no indicator.
claims.incremental_contribution: Matches the ratified Jet browser corner strip, still unbuilt.

claims.claim: Next lets users hide the indicator but never hides compile or runtime errors.
claims.incremental_contribution: A rule the Jet dashboard should keep: toggles hide chrome, not failures.

claims.claim: Next compiles routes lazily on first request to cut start time and memory; jet dev compiles the whole program before serving.
claims.incremental_contribution: One reason Next starts in about 200 ms of server work; for Jet, incremental compile (#2756/#6544) is the lever, not laziness.

claims.claim: Next documents environment slowdowns (antivirus, Gatekeeper, Docker file sharing, WSL /mnt/c) as the first troubleshooting step.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet docs have no dev performance troubleshooting page.

claims.claim: Next warns that polling-based watching "adds significant latency and can drastically increase CPU and I/O usage."
claims.incremental_contribution: Incumbent evidence against periodic polling; relevant to the ratified 400 ms dashboard poll.

claims.claim: Next caches server fetch results across hot reloads so edits do not refetch paid APIs.
claims.incremental_contribution: Analogue of Jet #Persist keeping state across reruns.

claims.claim: Next can log every server fetch with timing and cache status in the dev terminal; jet dev logs no requests at all.
claims.incremental_contribution: Request and outbound fetch logs are part of the same missing request log.

claims.claim: Turbopack tracing records per-module compile time and serves a trace viewer.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet has jet perf traces; a per-phase dev rebuild trace would explain the 1.5 s edit cycle.

claims.claim: Parcel docs promise a fallback port when 1234 is taken, but with an explicit -p we saw `Error: Port "5440" could not be used` with a stack trace.
claims.incremental_contribution: Even incumbents differ between docs and behavior; Jet should say plainly which port failed and what to do.

claims.claim: Parcel binds all interfaces and allows cross-origin requests by default; Vite defaults CORS to localhost origins only.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's 127.0.0.1 bind is the safer default; CORS policy for jet dev was not probed.

claims.claim: Parcel's module.hot.dispose(data)/accept carries state from the old module to the new one; React Fast Refresh keeps component state (we saw 0 reloads, state kept).
claims.incremental_contribution: Same shape as Jet's ratified #Persist handoff (D-DEV-STATE1) but for browser UI.

claims.claim: Parcel --lazy builds pages only when first requested, like Next's on-demand compile.
claims.incremental_contribution: Same lever as NL1; recorded for completeness.

claims.claim: Parcel's disk cache keys on files, config, plugins and dev dependencies, so a restarted dev server only rebuilds changes.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's content-addressed store plays this role; whether jet dev reuses it across restarts was not measured.

claims.claim: Parcel (.proxyrc), Vite (server.proxy) and Rsbuild (server.proxy) proxy API paths to another server during dev; jet dev has none.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet serves front and back from one process, so the need is smaller; low priority.

claims.claim: Parcel, Vite and Rsbuild let users add dev-only middleware; Jet routes are ordinary app code so a dev hook is less needed.
claims.incremental_contribution: Low priority; no card.

claims.claim: Parcel tells users to turn off editor safe-write because rename-on-save hides changes from its watcher.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's spec already requires the watcher to settle on content (in-place and rename saves); no Jet docs tell users to change editors.

claims.claim: Parcel documents the Linux inotify watch limit error and the sysctl fix.
claims.incremental_contribution: jet dev on a large tree may hit the same limit; no Jet message was seen for it.

claims.claim: Parcel installs missing plugins during dev automatically.
claims.incremental_contribution: An anti-lesson for Jet: silent installs during dev conflict with locked, reviewed dependencies.

claims.claim: Rsbuild serves /rsbuild-dev-server listing every built asset; jet dev has no page showing what it built or serves.
claims.incremental_contribution: Fits under the ratified /__jet_dev_status surface.

claims.claim: Rsbuild and Vite SPA fallback serve index.html (200) for unknown paths; jet dev answers 404 "no web route matches `/nope`".
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's typed 404 is clearer for server-routed apps.

claims.claim: Rsbuild offers three ways to add middleware (config, plugin hook, JS API).
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet routes are code; no dev middleware layer is proposed.

claims.claim: Rsbuild layers updates: HMR, then full live reload, then none; jet dev web pages get none of these (no browser update after edit).
claims.incremental_contribution: Live reload is the floor every incumbent provides; Jet ratified it (D-WEBAPP-SERVE1) under #4275 c82.

claims.claim: Rsbuild and Vite let users set the HMR WebSocket URL so updates work behind reverse proxies.
claims.incremental_contribution: A push channel needs this knob; a poll needs none. Input to the push-vs-poll ballot.

claims.claim: Vite tries the next port unless --strictPort is set, then prints the real URL; jet dev panics inside corelib (Web.jet:405 "os error 98") and never prints a URL.
claims.incremental_contribution: Port conflict UX: say which port is taken and either move with a printed URL or stop with a fix line.

claims.claim: Vite has --debug [feat] with --filter and --logLevel; jet dev's --verbose did nothing visible.
claims.incremental_contribution: A filterable debug channel would serve the ratified --verbose dashboard mode.

claims.claim: Vite pre-bundles npm dependencies so the browser makes one request per package; Jet web output is one wasm module plus jet_dom_runtime.js with no per-module requests.
claims.incremental_contribution: The whole pre-bundling problem does not exist for Jet; a structural lead.

claims.claim: Vite's dependency cache keys on the lockfile, config and NODE_ENV and is forced with --force.
claims.incremental_contribution: Explicit cache keys and a force flag; Jet's store is content-addressed (#2514) so no force flag is needed [INFERENCE].

claims.claim: Vite serves dependencies with immutable cache headers in dev; jet dev answered with Connection: close and no cache headers in our probe.
claims.incremental_contribution: Repeat page loads in jet dev refetch everything; minor until pages grow.

claims.claim: Vite replaces import.meta.env.DEV/PROD statically so dev-only code is removed from builds.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's dev-only blocks were not probed here; recorded as an evidence gap.

claims.claim: Vite, Bun and Next load .env files automatically in dev with a documented priority; jet dev loads none [INFERENCE: no .env handling found in the dev path].
claims.incremental_contribution: Env ownership belongs to the web platform card.

claims.claim: Vite types env only by user-written declaration augmentation, and values stay strings.
claims.incremental_contribution: A Jet typed config would beat this; none designed for env yet.

claims.claim: Vite's HMR keeps React state across edits (we saw count=3 survive, 0 reloads); jet dev gives the browser no update at all.
claims.incremental_contribution: State-keeping browser updates are the incumbent default; Jet's planned order is live reload first, then #Persist handoff.

claims.claim: Vite explicitly does not type check during dev; jet dev showed a checked type error (E0113) with Why/Fix in the terminal.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet lead; but the error never reaches the browser, where Vite and Next show an overlay.

claims.claim: Vite promises HMR under 50 ms; we measured 41 ms edit-to-browser vs 1525 ms edit-to-server for jet dev.
claims.incremental_contribution: Same gap the #2756 gauntlet tracks.

claims.claim: Vite treats every HTML file as a page entry; Jet maps pages with web.app().route(...) in code.
claims.incremental_contribution: Both give multi-page apps; Jet's routes are typed code.

claims.claim: Vite, Parcel and Rsbuild apply CSS edits without a reload; whether a jet dev .assets() CSS edit reaches the browser was not probed.
claims.incremental_contribution: Recorded as an evidence gap for the dashboard card.

claims.claim: Vite imports .wasm as an ES module or via ?init; Jet web output loads its own wasm through jet_dom_runtime.js without a bundler.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet owns the whole wasm path; no interop gap for jet dev.

claims.claim: Vite bundles web workers from new Worker(new URL(...)); Jet #Target(Web) worker support was not probed.
claims.incremental_contribution: Recorded as an evidence gap.

claims.claim: Vite supports CSP nonces on injected tags in dev and build; whether Jet's hydration scripts work under a strict CSP was not probed.
claims.incremental_contribution: Recorded as an evidence gap for #Target(Web).

claims.claim: Vite can emit a license file for bundled dependencies.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet's dependency audit (jet audit) could emit the same; low priority.

claims.claim: Vite moves to the next port and prints the new Local URL (we saw "Port 5401 is in use, trying another one..." then 5402).
claims.incremental_contribution: Moving is safe only because the URL is printed; jet dev prints none.

claims.claim: Vite restricts dev CORS to loopback origins after a security fix; Jet's dev server CORS behavior was not probed.
claims.incremental_contribution: Recorded as an evidence gap next to allowedHosts.

claims.claim: Vite, Next, Bun, Astro, Rsbuild and Parcel draw a compile-error overlay in the page (Vite can turn it off); jet dev drops the server so the browser shows "This site can't be reached".
claims.incremental_contribution: Top visual gap; the ratified overlay over the last good build fixes it.

claims.claim: Vite's HMR client falls back to a direct WebSocket when a reverse proxy breaks it, and documents the browser error that follows.
claims.incremental_contribution: A push channel must ship this fallback; the ratified status endpoint poll is a natural fallback.

claims.claim: Vite forwards browser errors and console warnings to the terminal, turned on automatically for AI coding agents.
claims.incremental_contribution: Agents and humans both need browser failures in the terminal; jet dev has none.

claims.claim: Vite can transform listed files at start so the first page load is fast.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet compiles everything first, so the first load is already warm; no gap.

claims.claim: Vite warns that polling watchers cost high CPU and documents the WSL2 cross-filesystem blind spot.
claims.incremental_contribution: Second incumbent warning against polling; input to the push-vs-poll ballot.

claims.claim: Vite refuses to serve .env, private keys and certificates by default (fs.deny); Jet's .assets("public") scope was not probed for dotfiles.
claims.incremental_contribution: Recorded as an evidence gap for the web platform.

claims.claim: Vite and Next hide framework frames ("Show 5 ignore-listed frame(s)"); jet dev's port-conflict panic pointed at `<corelib>/Core/Web/Web.jet:405 in __app_serve` instead of the user's .serve() call.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet should blame the user frame, as Bun did for EADDRINUSE; #3720 c48 owns corelib paths.

claims.claim: jet dev prints only "watching <absolute dir> (Ctrl-C to stop)": no URL, no ready line, no timing, no version. Every incumbent prints the URL and a ready time (Vite "ready in 109 ms", Next "✓ Ready in 193ms", Bun "Bundled page in 33ms").
claims.incremental_contribution: The ratified address line (D-WEBAPP-SERVE1, "# serving http://127.0.0.1:8080 (live reload)") is unbuilt; first-hour users cannot find their page.

claims.claim: After an edit jet dev reruns the program but the open browser tab gets no update: no WebSocket, no poll, no reload (edit_browser_self_update_ms null).
claims.incremental_contribution: Live reload is the floor every incumbent provides; ratified, owned by #4275 c82, and the transport is the D-FE-DEVPUSH1 ballot question.

claims.claim: jet dev edit-to-new-server took 1525 ms; incumbents updated the browser in 22-122 ms (Parcel 22, Bun 24, Vite 41, Rsbuild 55, Astro 103, Next 122); Deno restart 261 ms.
claims.incremental_contribution: Confirms the #2756 gauntlet gap on a web app.

claims.claim: Any compile or runtime error stops the jet dev server, so the browser shows Chrome's "This site can't be reached"; incumbents keep serving and draw an overlay over the last good page (Bun dims it, Next shows "1 Issue").
claims.incremental_contribution: The ratified dashboard (serve last good build, overlay with the verbatim diagnostic) is the fix; no implementation card exists.

claims.claim: One missing } produced five problems (E0003 x4 + E0083); Vite and Next showed one error with the opener and closer marked.
claims.incremental_contribution: Owned by #3720 c28-29.

claims.claim: jet dev resident memory was about 999 MB (app child 1.5 MB) vs Vite 274, Rsbuild 376, Astro 559, Parcel 581, Bun 83, Deno 79, Next about 1006 MB.
claims.incremental_contribution: The compiler side, not the app, holds the memory; no card tracks jet dev RSS.

claims.claim: jet dev shows checked type errors with Why/Fix/More (E0113) on save; Vite, Bun, Parcel and Rsbuild do not type check at all in dev, and our type-error edit loaded fine in all of them.
claims.incremental_contribution: A real Jet lead; it only reaches the terminal, not the browser.

claims.claim: One request to a panicking route ended the whole jet dev server (/ 200, /about 000, then every request 000 until the next save); Bun, Deno and Next answered 500 and kept serving.
claims.incremental_contribution: Direct evidence for #4635 c1.

claims.claim: A taken port made jet dev panic inside corelib (Web.jet:405, "os error 98"); Vite and Rsbuild moved to the next port and printed it, Astro named the running server's URL and PID, Bun pointed at the user's serve( line.
claims.incremental_contribution: Owned by #4635 c2 plus #3720 c14/c48.

claims.claim: The E3001 Why/Fix text reads "The shared report boundary owns the program-side stop" and lists exit codes 70/1/101, which tells a web developer nothing about the failing request.
claims.incremental_contribution: Owned by #3720 c14.

claims.claim: `fn dev(d: Dev) { d.serve(port: 5313) }` crashes the compiler ("internal compiler error ... entry function dev must take no parameters and return nothing"), and the shipped Examples/features/devloop/dev_context fails the same way.
claims.incremental_contribution: Contradicts ratified D-ENTRY-SHAPE1 (`fn dev(d: Dev)` is the documented shape); no card found.

claims.claim: jet dev --port 5317 reads 5317 as a file (E2105 "Can't securely read the file"); --open and an invented --bogusflag are accepted silently.
claims.incremental_contribution: Unknown flags must be refused; --port must parse (D-SETTING-ORDER1). #3720 c15 and #5069 own it.

claims.claim: Unbuilt jet dev forms report the wrong thing: --canvas says "`jet dev` is not built yet" (plain jet dev works) and --swap/--target say "`jet run --swap|--target` is not built yet"; jet help dev advertises all of them.
claims.incremental_contribution: Misleading refusals; no card found.

claims.claim: Typed h, r, o, q are echoed as ordinary input; Ctrl-C exits 130 without a closing line. Vite, Rsbuild and Astro list key shortcuts; Expo has single keys.
claims.incremental_contribution: Ratified session keys (D-RUN-SESSION1) are unbuilt; #2756 c3 contradicts them (D-DEV-KEYS1 ballot draft).

claims.claim: `jet new demo --template web` (0.17 s) ends with "next: cd demo && jet dev", but jet dev on the template serves nothing and jet run exits 0 silently.
claims.incremental_contribution: First-hour dead end; owned by #4275 c82 and the jet-web-template-loop card draft.

claims.claim: `jet build --target web` printed nothing and wrote no index.html.
claims.incremental_contribution: No card found; incumbents always summarize build output.

claims.claim: The reference app Examples/features/web/jet_web stops at start with E3001 "panic: id field" (run.jet:160).
claims.incremental_contribution: Owned by #6552.

claims.claim: jet dev idled at about 17 ms CPU per 10 s, the app child used 1.5 MB, and responses took under 1 ms; jet dev binds 127.0.0.1.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet leads on idle cost, app footprint and a safe default bind.

claims.claim: jet dev logs no requests; Next prints " GET / 200 in 213ms (next.js: 116ms, application-code: 98ms)" and Astro "[200] / 12ms".
claims.incremental_contribution: The ratified dashboard has a request list; no card builds it.

claims.claim: jet dev output is monochrome under a TTY (3 escape bytes in the whole log), while every incumbent colors errors, URLs and timings.
claims.incremental_contribution: Low impact; colour with NO_COLOR/--color is already a flag (--color in jet help dev).

claims.claim: Vite's banner gives version, ready time, Local URL, a hint for LAN, and the help key in four lines.
claims.incremental_contribution: Template for Jet's ready line.

claims.claim: Vite updated the browser 41 ms after a save with React state kept and no reload, from a 274 MB process.
claims.incremental_contribution: Benchmark for #2756 and #6386.

claims.claim: Vite's syntax overlay shows the file, line, a framed snippet and the plugin name, and the terminal repeats it with a JS stack.
claims.incremental_contribution: Overlay content model for the Jet dashboard.

claims.claim: A React render error in Vite left a blank white page and nothing in the terminal (no overlay by default for runtime errors).
claims.incremental_contribution: Incumbents are not uniformly good; Next, Bun and Parcel did show runtime overlays.

claims.claim: Next prints both the Local and the LAN Network URL at start because it binds 0.0.0.0.
claims.incremental_contribution: Shows the convenience Jet trades for a safe default; Jet should print the LAN URL only under --share lan.

claims.claim: Next logs every request with status and a split of framework vs application time.
claims.incremental_contribution: Best request log seen; model for the Jet dashboard request list.

claims.claim: A render-time TypeError in Next produced a 500 with an overlay naming the user frame while the server kept serving other routes.
claims.incremental_contribution: Contrast with the jet dev handler panic.

claims.claim: Creating a Next app took about 50 s and 360 packages with 16 reported vulnerabilities; `jet new --template web` took 0.17 s with zero dependencies.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet lead on setup weight and supply chain.

claims.claim: Next stops on a taken port with "⨯ Failed to start server" and a raw Node error object, without suggesting another port.
claims.incremental_contribution: Even the market leader prints internals here; Astro's message is the better model.

claims.claim: Astro logs each request as "[status] path time" (e.g. "[404] /nope 3ms").
claims.incremental_contribution: Minimal request log worth matching.

claims.claim: Astro's page edit caused a full browser reload (103 ms) and lost client state, like a plain live reload.
claims.incremental_contribution: Shows live reload without state is still acceptable to a mainstream framework; Jet's first step can be the same.

claims.claim: Astro's second dev server names the running server's URL and PID and offers stop or --force.
claims.incremental_contribution: Best port-conflict message captured; model for #4635 c2.

claims.claim: Astro's CompilerError overlay showed "An error occurred." plus an internal Vite stack-rewrite warning.
claims.incremental_contribution: Anti-lesson: overlays must show the user's diagnostic, not tool internals; Jet's ratified verbatim diagnostic avoids this.

claims.claim: Rsbuild prints "start build started..." and "ready built in 0.05s" for each rebuild.
claims.incremental_contribution: Per-rebuild status line matches the ratified two-row Jet header content.

claims.claim: Rsbuild updated the browser 55 ms after a save with state kept.
claims.incremental_contribution: Second Rust-based data point for #2756.

claims.claim: Rsbuild moves to the next free port with one info line naming both ports.
claims.incremental_contribution: Clear, short conflict handling.

claims.claim: Parcel had the fastest browser update measured, 22 ms, with React state kept.
claims.incremental_contribution: Upper bound of what users now expect.

claims.claim: Parcel's runtime overlay collapses 22 framework frames and keeps the user frame with a code snippet.
claims.incremental_contribution: Same rule as ignore-listing: blame the user's line first.

claims.claim: Bun started in 160 ms at about 83 MB resident and printed the bundle time for the page.
claims.incremental_contribution: Lowest footprint of the JavaScript incumbents; shows a dev server need not cost 1 GB.

claims.claim: Bun keeps the last good page visible but dimmed under a build-error card that only fixing can dismiss.
claims.incremental_contribution: Exactly the ratified Jet behavior (dim, overlay, serve last good build), already shipping elsewhere.

claims.claim: A throwing Bun handler returned a 500 dev page and logged "GET - /api/hello/boom failed", and the next request got 200.
claims.incremental_contribution: Evidence for #4635 c1.

claims.claim: Bun's port conflict points at the user's serve({ line and asks "Is port 5450 in use?"
claims.incremental_contribution: Blames user code, not runtime internals; model for Jet.

claims.claim: deno serve --watch uses the same restart model as jet dev (no browser update, server restarts) but restarts in 261 ms and prints the listening URL.
claims.incremental_contribution: Closest incumbent to Jet; shows the restart model can be fast and still print the address.

claims.claim: Like jet dev, deno serve --watch drops the server on a syntax error (ECONNREFUSED) and waits for the next save.
claims.incremental_contribution: Jet is not alone in going down, but every bundler-based incumbent keeps serving.

claims.claim: Deno's port conflict prints "AddrInUse ... (os error 98)" with an internal ext:deno_net frame, much like jet dev's corelib frame.
claims.incremental_contribution: Shared weakness; Bun and Astro show the better message.
